title: “Hamam böcekleri” sokaktan çekilmedi, Eğitim Bakanı istifa etti
content:
Hindistan Eğitim Bakanı Dharmendra Pradhan, ülke genelinde haftalardır devam eden öğrenci protestolarının ardından 25 Temmuz Cumartesi günü istifa etti.


Pradhan, kararını sosyal medya hesabından duyurdu ve istifa mektubunu Başbakan Narendra Modi’ye sunduğunu açıkladı. İstifa, Modi hükümetinin protestoların başlamasından bu yana attığı ilk önemli geri adım olarak değerlendirildi.


Hindistan’da “Hamam Böceği Halk Partisi” isyanı: Gençler neden sokakta?


23 Temmuz 2026


Protestolar sınavlardaki usulsüzlük iddialarıyla başladı


“Cockroach Janta Party” — Türkçesiyle “Hamam böceği Halk Partisi” — adıyla örgütlenen hareket, üniversite ve kamu sınavlarında soru sızdırıldığı ve sonuçların usulsüz biçimde değiştirildiği iddialarının ardından başladı.


Başlangıçta eğitim sisteminin yeniden düzenlenmesini isteyen hareket, zamanla genç işsizliği, ekonomik fırsat eşitsizliği ve kamu görevlilerinin hesap vermesi gibi talepleri de gündemine aldı. Öğrencilerin yanı sıra aileler, çalışanlar ve hak savunucuları da Yeni Delhi ve farklı kentlerdeki gösterilere katıldı.


Hareketin adı, Hindistan’daki üst düzey bir yargıcın işsiz gençler için kullandığı “hamam böceği” ifadesinin protestocular tarafından sahiplenilmesine dayanıyor. İnternet ortamında hiciv amacıyla ortaya çıkan hareket, daha sonra kitlesel sokak eylemlerine dönüştü.


Türkiye, pestisit nedeniyle Hindistan’dan sonra en çok bildirim alan ikinci ülke


13 Ocak 2026


Polis müdahalesinde öğrenciler yaralandı


Yeni Delhi’de parlamentoya yürümek isteyen binlerce kişiye polis cop ve göz yaşartıcı gazla müdahale etti. Müdahalede çok sayıda öğrenci yaralandı. Protestolar oturma eylemleri ve açlık grevleriyle devam etti.


Hükümet daha önce sınav yolsuzluklarıyla ilgili davaların hızlandırılacağını ve sınav sistemindeki usulsüzlüklere karşı yeni düzenlemeler yapılacağını açıklamıştı. Protestocular ise bu adımların sorumluların hesap vermesi için yeterli olmadığını belirterek Pradhan’ın istifasını istemişti.


Eylemler sürecek


İstifa kararının ardından Yeni Delhi’deki eylem alanında kutlamalar yapıldı. Hareket, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada “Demokrasi kazandı” dedi.


Protestocular, Pradhan’ın istifasına rağmen eylemleri sona erdirmeyeceklerini duyurdu. Hareketin kalan talepleri arasında sınav sızıntılarının ardından yaşamına son veren öğrencilerin ailelerine tazminat ödenmesi, eylemlere katılanlara cezai işlem uygulanmaması ve polis müdahaleleri hakkında soruşturma açılması bulunuyor.


(NÖ)

author: CNT Aragón-Rioja
title: CNT Zaragoza denuncia ante Inspección de Trabajo el accidente laboral de un afiliado en HARINAS POLO
content:
La histórica harinera de Villanueva del Gállego, Harinas Polo, ha sido denunciada ante Inspección de Trabajo por el accidente laboral ocurrido en la sección de ‘minoritarios’ en febrero de este 2026, con la caída de un trabajador por las escaleras de la mezcladora.

En la Denuncia, puesta por el trabajador accidentado – afiliado a CNT -, se señala el mal estado de ésta y otras zonas del centro, donde los trabajadores y trabajadoras han tenido caídas, resbalones, o golpes que no han acabado en baja por pura suerte. En opinión del sindicato y tal y como expresa la denuncia,

 no es normal el gran número de accidentes que ocurren en Harinas Polo, y la plantilla se está jugando la salud en todas las secciones por la falta de mantenimiento y renovación de material

 y zonas de trabajo.


Desde CNT hemos ofrecido una reunión a la Dirección de Harinas Polo para tratar los temas de esta denuncia ante Inspección, y si algún trabajador de cualquier sección quiere que le traslademos otro problema puede comunicarse con nosotros.

También

 ofrecemos nuestros SERVICIOS JURÍDICOS GRATUITOS si algún trabajador del sector de Harinas y Sémolas quiere revisar su situación

 o directamente asesorarse para denunciar el mal estado de algún material o zona, o accidentes pasados. Puedes escribir al sindicato ( zaragoza@cnt.es 694468898 ) si tienes cualquier duda.


Por nuestra salud, nuestra seguridad y por un trabajo digno, ¡afíliate a CNT!

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Milagro Sala: “La quieren ver muerta”
content:
La Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos (Corte IDH) levantó las medidas provisionales que la protegían desde 2017. Aún así, sostiene que las condiciones de detención de la dirigente de la Tupac Amaru no deberían modificarse.


“La quieren ver muerta y estamos dando una batalla para que no la maten”, manifestó su médico Jorge Rachid tras conocerse la novedad judicial. “El acoso judicail va a aumentar después de que la CIDH bajó la cautelar. Esto realmente nos alarma”, agregó Rachid.


La CIDH dio por terminada la medida cautelar que protegía a la dirigente social en una resolución publicada el 3 de juliio. Si bien el organismo considera que el riesgo clínico para la vida y la integridad de Milagro Sala se mantiene igual que antes, entiende que el Estado argentino está dando una respuesta efectiva y garantiza los tratamientos y traslados (sic).


Sin embargo, a comienzos de este año, el gobierno nacional pidió el levantamiento de las medidas de protección para enviarla a una cárcel común.


“Cualquier intento de trasladar a Milagro a un establecimiento penitenciario o de alejarla del tratamiento que hoy la sostiene sería contarrio a lo que la CIDH estableció (“El levantamiento de las presentes medidas no debe entenderse como una habilitación para revertir, sin justificación, las condiciones internas de protección actualmente existentes”) y comprometería directamente su vida. La resolución no habilita ningún retroceso sino que obliga al Estado a sostener la protección.


Milagro Sala junto a Jorge Rachid el 14 de octubre de 2023, al retirarse del Hospital Italiano de La Plata tras una internación de diez días


“El cuerpo de Milagro está diciéndonos que no da más”


Milagro permanece en la cama, casi no se levanta ni come. No quiere recibir ni hablar con nadie y su salud es delicada. Al conocerse la gravedad de su estado, organizaciones políticas, sociales, sindicales y de Derechos Humanos realizaron una conferencia de prensa para reclamar su liberación. Allí Rachid dio detalles de cómo le salvaron la vida al trasladarla a La Plata y del hostigamiento que todavía sufre por parte de la justicia de Jujuy, que envió dos comisiones de fiscales, médicos y psicólogos para intentar indagarla y abrir nuevas causas judiciales.


El médico pidió hacer responsables al Poder Judicial jujeño y a la Corte Suprema de Justicia por convalidar la persecución y consideró necesario que “paguen el daño que le están haciendo a una líder que está presa por ser mujer, por ser negra por ser que chua, por ser dirigente sindical y por tener lo que hay que tener, que hoy le está faltando a mucha dirigencia política”.


María Elena Naddeo, secretaria general de la APDH, fue ortra de las oradoras de esa conferencia, que se realizó en el auditorio de ATE, y admitió la impotencia que le genera la situación de Milagro. “No sabemos más qué hacer. El cuerpo de Milagro está diciéndonos que no da más. Por eso tenemos que ir por su libertad”, señaló y añadió: “Hoy Milagro Sala se quiere dejar morir y no lo podemos permitir. Por eso hoy reclamamos con urgencia su libertad”, añadió.


Lanzan una campaña global ante su grave estado de salud


​En un colmado auditorio de la Asociación de Trabajadores del Estado (ATE) Capital, un amplio arco de dirigentes políticos, sociales, religiosos y de Derechos Humanos encabezó una conferencia de prensa de urgencia para denunciar el drástico deterioro en la salud de Milagro Sala. Bajo la consigna de que la persecución judicial en su contra se ha transformado en una “condena de muerte silenciosa”, los referentes exigieron al gobierno nacional un trato humanitario inmediato y su urgente liberación. La actividad fue impulsada por el foro internacional Sovitern (Red Internacional del Nuevo Socialismo del Siglo XXI), bajo la coordinación general de Lois Pérez Leira, y el manifiesto por la urgente libertad de la líder de la Tupac Amaru ya cuenta con más de 3.000 firmas de apoyo provenientes de todo el mundo. Desde la organización advirtieron que la campaña internacional no cesará hasta lograr que Sala sea liberada de manera definitiva.


Imagen:

Sovintern


​La mesa y la moderación de la conferencia de prensa estuvieron coordinadas por Fernanda Pereyra, abogada y militante, quien fue la encargada de articular los discursos y las fuertes adhesiones políticas. El acto se convirtió en una caja de resonancia de la militancia popular y sumó respaldos internacionales de peso como los de Evo Morales (Bolivia), Manuel Zelaya y …

title: Ceyda Sungur: "Mekansal okuryazarlık içinde bulunduğumuz düzeni sorgulamayı gerektiriyor"
content:
Atölye BİA'nın 25-26 Temmuz’da gerçekleştirilen Mekansal Okuryazarlık Atölyesi'nin ilk gününde Ceyda Sungur, “Mekansal Okuryazarlığa Giriş” ve “Toplumsal Mekanın Üretimi” başlıklı iki oturum gerçekleştirdi. 


Sungur, ilk oturumda katılımcılarla birlikte mekansal okuryazarlığın ne anlama geldiğini tartıştı. Mekanı yalnızca fiziksel özellikleriyle değil, toplumsal hafıza, gündelik yaşam, sınıfsal ilişkiler ve kentteki dönüşümler üzerinden ele aldı. 


Katılımcılar, mekan ve hafıza ilişkisini farklı örnekler üzerinden inceledi. Binaların mimarları, kapı zilleri, kentsel dönüşümle küçülen evler ve mahallelerde değişen ticari yapılar bu örnekler arasındaydı. 


Tanıma, tanışma ve dönüştürme 


Sungur, mekansal okuryazarlığı “tanıma, tanışma ve dönüştürme” süreci olarak tarif etti. Bir mekanın fiziksel özelliklerini fark etmenin “tanıma” aşaması olduğunu söyledi. Mekanın taşıdığı toplumsal ilişkileri sorgulamaya başlamanın ise tanımayı “tanışmaya” dönüştürdüğünü anlattı. 


Sungur, mekansal okuryazarlığın kişinin kendi konumunu ve içinde bulunduğu toplumsal ilişkileri sorgulamasını da beraberinde getirdiğine dikkat çekti.  


Kendi sınıfsal pozisyonumuzu ve sınıfın tarihsel olarak kendi mekanını nasıl ürettiğini sorgulamaya başladığımızda bir dönüşüm sürecine giriyoruz. Edindiğimiz bilgi ve becerileri eleştirel düşünceden geçirerek bir yurttaşlık pratiğine dönüştürüyoruz. Kişinin içinde bulunduğu ve dönüştürmeye çalıştığı düzen içinde farklı bir özne haline gelmesini, buradaki adaletsizlikler üzerinden bir hak arama süreci başlatmasını da dönüştürme eylemi olarak tarif ediyorum. 


Sungur, bu çerçevede mekansal okuryazarlığın kişinin mekanla ve çevresindeki toplumsal ilişkilerle kurduğu ilişkiyi yeniden düşünmesine imkan verdiğini vurguladı. 


 


 


 


 


 


Bu gönderiyi Instagram'da gör


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


Atölye BİA (@atolyebia)'in paylaştığı bir gönderi


Mekan toplumsal ilişkilerle nasıl üretiliyor? 


Günün ikinci oturumu “Toplumsal Mekanın Üretimi” başlığıyla devam etti. Sungur, bu kez tartışmayı “Neden mekan değil de toplumsal mekan diyoruz?” sorusuyla açtı. 


Katılımcılar bu soruyu hafıza, sosyalleşme, eşitlik, güvenli alan ve farklı toplumsal grupların mekanla kurduğu ilişkiler üzerinden tartıştı. 


Sungur, mekanın yalnızca fiziksel bir alan olmadığını vurguladı. Toplumsal ilişkilerin mekan içinde kurulduğunu, bu ilişkilerin aynı zamanda mekanı dönüştürdüğünü anlattı. Böylece mekanın sürekli üretilen ve yeniden üretilen bir süreç olduğunu söyledi. 


Bu süreçte fiziksel çevrenin yanı sıra sosyoekonomik koşulların, kültürün, kimliğin, toplumsal cinsiyetin ve iktidar ilişkilerinin de rol oynadığını belirtti. Mekanı oluşturan bu düzeylerin birbirinden ayrı düşünülemeyeceğini aktardı. 


Kadınlar mekanı nasıl deneyimliyor? 


Oturumda mekanın toplumsal cinsiyete göre nasıl farklı deneyimlendiği de tartışıldı. Katılımcılar, evden sokağa ve işyerine uzanan gündelik deneyimlerden örnekler verdi. 


Tartışma sırasında ev içi emeğin mekanla ilişkisi de gündeme geldi. Sungur, kadınlara atfedilen toplumsal rollerin evin deneyimlenme biçimini de belirlediğine dikkat çekti: 


Kadınlara toplumsal olarak atfedilmiş rollerin en çok ve en görünmez şekilde gerçekleştiği yerlerden biri ev. Ev içi emek de bu gündelik pratiklerin bir parçası. Bu nedenle ev, kadınlar için daha fazla emek harcanan ve farklı deneyimlenen bir mekan haline geliyor.


Sungur, toplumsal cinsiyet ilişkilerinin işyerindeki deneyimleri de şekillendirdiğini söyledi. İşçi ve işveren arasındaki hiyerarşinin, kadınlara ve erkeklere atfedilen rollerle birleştiğinde bir baskı aracına dönüşebildiğini belirtti. 


Mekan kimin için tasarlanıyor? 


Sungur, mekanın nasıl planlandığı ve tasarlandığına da dikkat çekti. Kaldırımların genişliğinden kentte hareket etmeyi belirleyen standartlara kadar birçok kararın, hangi bedenlerin hesaba katıldığını gösterdiğini anlattı. 


Kaldırım örneği üzerinden “standart” kabul edilen bedenin kim olduğu tartışıldı. Kaldırımın tekerlekli sandalye kullanan birinin, elinde poşet taşıyan birinin ya da yan yana hareket eden iki kişinin kullanımına uygun olup olmadığı sorgulandı. 


Sungur, bu örneklerle mekanın tasarlanma biçiminin bazı bedenlerin hareketini kolaylaştırırken bazılarını sınırlandırabildiğine dikkat çekti. 


Bir domates bize ne anlatır? 


Sungur, oturumun devamında katılımcılarla gündelik bir nesneden yola çıkarak mekanın üretim süreçlerini sorgulamaya yönelik bir egzersiz yaptı.  …

author: antimilitarismus
title: Ani válka, ani „mír“ – revoluce
content:
// Anti-militarist initiative // Antimilitarista Kezdeményezés // Antimilitaristische initiative // Антимілітаристська ініціатива //

Dnes již nemůžeme ignorovat skutečnost, že války, masakry a genocidy se šíří a stupňují všude: v Kongu, Súdánu, Jemenu, Myanmaru, Palestině, na Ukrajině, v Íránu, Libanonu… Vlády si stále vymýšlejí výmluvy pro bombardování: útočit v sebeobraně, zabíjet za účelem ochrany, útočit za účelem osvobození…

V Evropě měla svou chvíli slávy rétorika o takzvaném „věčném míru“ po skončení studené války. Dnes se militaristická propaganda vrací: vojáci navštěvují školy, aby propagovali své povolání; všude je vidět propagandu obrany, na ulicích, na internetu i v kinech; dopis Théo Franckena [ministra obrany a zahraničního obchodu] adresovaný všem sedmnáctiletým, který je vyzývá k dobrovolnému vstupu do armády; rady ohledně survival kitů; a tak dále… Všude vnucují myšlenku, že se člověk musí připravit na válku, připravit se na boj, připravit se na „ztrátu dětí“. Je válka u konce? Nedokážeme si představit jinou možnou perspektivu?

Válka je údělem kapitalismu, ne naším!

Protože když se kapitalistický systém ocitne v krizi, válka je jedním z „řešení“, které ekonomickému systému poskytuje mechanismus ničení a sociální kontroly.

Kapitalistický systém potřebuje válku z mnoha důvodů. „Zajistit“ a přivlastnit si území; kontrolovat přírodní zdroje; odvést pozornost obyvatelstva od rostoucího vnitřního politického napětí a bídných životních podmínek; vytvořit „jednotu“ tváří v tvář vnějšímu nepříteli a posílit vlastenectví; disciplinovat obyvatelstvo, včetně marginalizace a potlačování těch, kteří jsou považováni za hrozbu; potlačovat revoluce a sociální hnutí, jako například v Sýrii nebo Súdánu; posílit státní struktury, dohled a zvýšit vojenské rozpočty, čímž se vytváří „válečná ekonomika“, která je velmi užitečná v obdobích bez konfliktů na vlastním území. Válka je výnosná. Pokud existuje někdo, kdo z válek vždy vychází jako vítěz, je to zbrojní průmysl!

Válka nikdy nebude v našem zájmu a jelikož systém bez ní nemůže přežít, je nutné najít řešení: zničit tento systém!

Je nezbytné bojovat zde, vlastními prostředky a v našem měřítku: organizovat se bez autorit, decentralizovat boj, posílit sebe a posílit boje proti státu.

Sabotovat válečný stroj; stavět se proti válkám států; podporovat dezertéry z celého světa; solidaritu s boji a povstáními; útočit na zbrojní průmysl; odmítat účast na válečném úsilí; vzdorovat propagandě; šířit antimilitaristické myšlenky; hájit internacionalistickou perspektivu.

Tváří v tvář zákonu silnějšího se bráníme solidaritou a vzájemnou pomocí. Tváří v tvář rozkazu bránit tento systém proti vnějšímu nepříteli se bráníme útokem na ty, kteří nás utlačují. Tváří v tvář stroji smrti bojujte za život ve svobodě.

Ani válka, ani „mír“ – revoluce!

Antimilitaristické shromáždění – Brusel

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Filipino children still oppressed under Marcos Jr. admin
content:
Child rights advocates hold puzzle pieces and break a chain, as part of their symbolic action after a July 23 forum at the Commission of Human Rights, Quezon City ahead of Marcos Jr.’s 2026 SONA. Photo by Elisha Beatrice Umali

“Instead of lowering [the minimum age of criminal responsibility], the government must ensure first that our children and youth are growing up in a safe environment, whether inside their homes, schools, and in the community.”

By Elisha Beatrice Umali Bulatlat.com

MANILA — The longstanding problems of a Filipino child continue to persist under the Marcos Jr. administration.

Different child rights organizations cited poverty, faulty basic education systems, lagging early childhood care and development (EECD), stunting and malnutrition, as well as systemic rights abuses as main issues children face in the country.

“Nine percent of Filipino children come from the working class and farmers that experience extreme poverty. This means that a child’s life is not separate from the lived realities of their families,” said Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns spokesperson m Elle Buntag.

A 2026 UNICEF study shows that 17.9 million children are living in poverty as of 2023, placed in the context of the international poverty line at (approximately $785.49 USD) per capita/year.

“A comparison of population and poverty shares of children and adults shows that children are over-represented among the poor. In 2023, children accounted for half of the poor population in the Philippines (50.5 per cent) even though they only accounted for a third of the total population (32.3 per cent),” the study pointed out.

In an interview with Bulatlat, Buntag said poverty remains the top problem of Filipino children. “As long as poverty remains in our country, there will be no good future for the children,” she said in Filipino.

Child development centers, expected to provide early childhood care, education and health services to children from birth to five years years, also face a backlog of approximately 33,000 as of 2024.

“Supposedly, all barangays should have child development centers but not all [barangays] have it. At the same time, not all parents are capable of enrolling their children to private schools providing childhood care and development,” Buntag explained.

Salinlahi also reported a 240,000 backlog in daycare workers nationwide. “Child development workers sometimes handle up to 20 kids, even though only a 1 worker to 10 kids is the ideal ratio,” added Buntag.

The basic education sector also faces backlogs. According to the Second Congressional Commission on Education (Edcom II), the country now faces over 166,000 in classroom backlogs with only 200 classrooms built per year.

Read: New school year, same problems

Edcom II’s findings also showed that students become less literate as they reach higher grade levels. “While improvements were observed in earlier grades in elementary, these appear to taper off in later grades, and especially in Grades 7 to 10, with many learners unable to become  independent readers as academic demands become more advanced,” stated the commission.

Rowena Legaspi of the Children’s Legal Rights and Development Center (CLDRC) criticized the current implementation of the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act (JJWA). While the law itself was strengthened in 2013, its implementation remained insufficient to support Children in Conflict with the Law (CICLs).

“The failure is in the implementers… Let’s ask them, what did you do for this law? What was your contribution to having an effective diversion program at the barangay level? As long as you do not have a contribution, do not push for the lowering of the criminal liability age,” said Legaspi.

Read: Child rights advocates oppose lowering criminal responsibility age

Read: Right(s) Up: Juvenile Justice Act pushes for restorative justice, offenders still face accountability

CLRDC’s latest data from 2023 to 2025 shows that most offenders are aged 15-17 years old. These offenders mostly commit serious offenses such as murder and rape.

Brochure given by CLRDC with the latest data on CICLs from years 2023 to 2025. Photo by Elisha Beatrice Umali

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Resolve the continuing Marawi displacement, Marcos Jr. urged
content:
Marawi war-displaced families and several organizations stage a protest action on May 23, 2026, in Marawi City in commemoration of the ninth year of the Marawi Siege, demanding their kambalingan (safe and dignified return). Photo from the Reclaiming Marawi Movement.

The prolonged and permanent displacement, long-overdue monetary compensation, and the dire situation of displaced families reflect “the true face of Marawi’s rehabilitation.”

CAGAYAN DE ORO — Ferdinand Marcos Jr. did not mention anything about Marawi rehabilitation during his State of the Nation Address (SONA) last year. Now, families displaced by the Marawi Siege in 2017 urged the current administration to put an end to their continuing displacement.

The Reclaiming Marawi Movement (RMM), a group led by internally displaced persons (IDPs) demanding for their immediate return, called on the Marcos Jr. administration to fast-track the release of the monetary compensation, which property owners are entitled to under the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act.

Many claimants have used their compensation for house repair, as reflected in a study conducted last year by the Marawi Compensation Board (MCB), the government body that awards monetary compensation.

MCB data revealed that a total of 3,699 claims were resolved from 2023 to June 30, 2026, amounting to P6.154 billion. This is 25.51 percent of the estimated 14,497 total claims to be resolved by the body by 2028.

Ramadan Muntor, RMM coordinator, told Bulatlat that many families currently living in temporary shelters have yet to receive their compensation. On the other hand, he called on Marcos Jr. that the provision of permanent shelters should be for all, including those sharers and renters displaced by the war.

“Their livelihoods are here,” he stressed.

Based on the available information gathered by Bulatlat from various government agencies and offices, at least more than 2,100 permanent housing shelters intended for Marawi displaced families were completely built in Marawi City and Lanao del Sur.

This is apart from the ongoing project constructions.

Marawi Advocacy Accompaniment, a coalition of IDPs and civil society groups, monitored around 17,000 families, or around 80,000 individuals, still living and surviving their dire situation in what it described as rusty and dilapidated temporary shelters in Marawi City and Lanao del Sur.

Read: After 9 years, Marawi displaced families have yet to return to their homes

While waiting for a livable relocation, RMM has been urging the government to spearhead the negotiation with the landowners of temporary shelters for extension to avoid any eviction threat. The government, Muntor said, should also at least extend assistance to repair the deteriorating shelters.

Read: Displaced Marawi residents face eviction from temporary shelter

Moreover, the group demanded an independent inquiry to know the circumstances that led to the destructive 2017 Marawi Siege. “People won’t be displaced without the war,” Muntor said.

Marawi City-based Moro Consensus Group earlier criticized the Rodrigo Duterte administration for using excessive force—through heavy bombardment—in dealing with the Islamic State-inspired Maute group.

On May 23, war-displaced families and support groups marked with a protest the ninth year of the five-month battle that ravaged the Islamic City, demanding their Kambalingan —a Meranaw term for dignified return.

Tirmizy Abdullah, a history professor from the Mindanao State University (MSU) in Marawi City and convenor of Marawi Advocacy Accompaniment, earlier said the prolonged and permanent displacement, long-overdue monetary compensation, and the dire situation of displaced families reflect “the true face of Marawi’s rehabilitation.” (RVO)

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: ‘Selective prosecution’ in Marcos Jr. anti-corruption probe?
content:
Human rights groups Karapatan and Alyansa Laban sa Korapsyon at Brutalidad ng Pulis (AKAB) hold a protest in front of Department of Justice on January 29, 2026, to condemn the sedition cases filed against anti-corruption activists who were present in last year's #BahaSaLuneta protest. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat

“Marcos is at the top, and those at the lower levels cannot be the only ones held accountable.”

CAGAYAN DE ORO — Since President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s “ mahiya naman kayo ” remarks at his State of the National Address (SONA) last year, who has been held accountable so far over the multibillion-peso flood control scam, the country’s so-called largest corruption scandal?

Among those detained so far are several officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), private contractors Curlee and Sarah Discaya, former senator Ramon “Bong” Revilla, and incumbent senator Jinggoy Estrada.

For ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio, however, those currently detained show selective prosecution as the the principal architects remain scot-free. “What if the biggest fish is President Marcos himself?”

In a video statement released in November 2025, former Ako Bicol Party-list representative and House appropriations committee chairperson Zaldy Co, one of the elected officials implicated over this mess, claimed that there were instructions given by Marcos Jr. to insert P100 billion worth of projects during the bicameral conference for the 2025 national budget.

Co also mentioned the participation of former budget secretary Amenah Pangandaman, former undersecretary Adrian Bersamin, and Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez.

TIMELINE: 2025 Flood Control Projects Corruption Scandal

Last year, Tinio and other lawmakers under the Makabayan bloc filed a resolution asking the now-defunct Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI), tasked to probe anomalies involving infrastructure projects, to investigate these officials, including former executive secretary Lucas Bersamin, presidential son Ilocos Norte 1st District Rep. Sandro Marcos, Justice Undersecretary Jose Cadiz, former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan, and other DPWH officials.

Tinio said that accountability remains elusive for officials close to Marcos Jr. He even appointed Pangandaman who resigned as budget secretary as the chairperson and chief executive officer (CEO) of the state-run Al-Amanah Islamic Investment Bank of the Philippines. Tinio also questioned the decision to make Bonoan a state witness, knowing that he led the DPWH when the anomalous flood control projects broke out.

Cadiz, who resigned last year after he was implicated, has returned to his post.

Pangandaman remains under investigation by the Office of the Ombudsman despite her appointment. Complaints against Romualdez and Sen. Joel Villanueva have reportedly reached the preliminary investigation stage.

Sen. Chiz Escudero who currently serves as the presiding officer for the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte also faced a plunder complaint over this scam which may be brought to court in weeks, according to Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla in June.

In a statement, the Kilusang Bayan Kontra Kurakot asked why charges have not yet been filed against them.

The ICI submitted its findings to the Ombudsman which included referrals for more than 60 individuals either for filing criminal and administrative charges or for further investigation.

Eight members of the House of Representatives and seven senators were included in the referral, according to an Inquirer report quoting Remulla.

Renato Reyes Jr., president of multisectoral group Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan), said that DPWH officials and the Discaya couple should not only be the ones prosecuted. He stressed that those who pushed for the pork barrel system and made the budget insertions, as well as signed and implemented the budget, should be investigated.

“Flood control and infrastructure corruption is a system. Marcos is at the top, and those at the lower levels cannot be the only ones held accountable,” Reyes wrote in a Facebook post in Filipino.

According to IBON Foundation’s estimate, P197 billion in public funds may have been lost annually to flood control corruption under the Marcos Jr. administration from 2023 to 2025. The amount, IBON said, is enough to procure more than 56,000 hospital beds, hire 200,000 nurses and more than 63,000 doctors, and establish more than 15,000 barangay …

author: Duda Sousa
title: As 48 horas que não existiram
content:
O tempo sempre me pareceu menos uma medida exata do que uma presença espessa. Como alguém que caminha ao nosso lado sem fazer alarde, mas que, num súbito arbítrio, decide apressar o passo ou deter-se de vez. Aprendi a tatear essa estranha relação ao observar duas histórias que desaguaram e se misturaram em mim.


No dia 24 de novembro, o médico chamou a mim e à minha mãe para conversar. O ar estava denso, não havia como desviar do que já se anunciava. Ele nos disse que “talvez vocês devessem se despedir do Sr. Carlos [meu pai], pois ele não deve resistir por muito mais tempo”. Aquela frase cavou um espaço oco e vagaroso no meu peito, como se o próprio tempo tivesse se esticado dolorosamente só para que eu pudesse sorver o peso dela.


E então, num mistério insondável, passaram exatamente trinta dias. Um mês inteiro em que o tempo resolveu, por algum motivo obscuro, ser generoso. Trinta dias de despedidas que nunca se fechavam por completo, de conversas que entrelaçavam esperança e aceitação, e de silêncios que diziam tudo. Eu sabia que estava perdendo meu pai, mas também sabia, com uma lucidez cortante, que ainda havia tempo. E recebi isso também como um gesto de gentileza.


Cresci aprendendo a ler o tempo também como um sinal. Sendo católica de berço, tenho o vício de decifrar as datas como uma espécie de “linguagem de Deus”. Meu pai nasceu no dia 22 de maio, dia de Santa Rita, a santa das causas impossíveis. Depois de 81 dias internado, por ter contraído uma síndrome rara enquanto tratava um câncer, ele recebeu alta no dia 19 de março, dia de São José, padroeiro das famílias e da boa morte, um cuidado simbólico.


E então ele morreu no dia 24 de dezembro, às vésperas do nascimento de Cristo. Às 15h da tarde, na hora da misericórdia, que dizem ter sido também a hora da morte de Cristo. Mais uma coincidência que nunca foi só coincidência para mim. Era como se o tempo, além de passar, também se ocupasse de tecer pequenos sentidos ao longo do caminho.


Mesmo assim, nada disso impede o que ele faz de mais inevitável: seguir.


Foi já nesse outro tempo, o do luto, que ouvi a Ana Paula Renault falar do

pai no Big Brother Brasil

, logo no início do reality show. Havia ali uma intimidade que eu reconhecia nas minhas próprias entranhas. Um jeito de falar que não era só de filha, mas também de melhor amiga. E então veio um acontecimento e um detalhe que ficaram cravados em mim como uma pergunta suspensa: dois dias.


Depois de mais de cem dias na casa, sem qualquer contato com o mundo exterior, faltavam apenas dois dias para o fim. Dois dias para que ela saísse, reencontrasse o pai e dividisse com ele o momento que tanto buscara ali. E o tempo não esperou; seguiu indiferente. O pai dela morreu dois dias antes da sua vitória no jogo.


Quando eu soube, logo pensei no quanto a vida fora cruel com ela naquele instante. Enquanto eu tive um mês, ela não teve dois dias. Desde então, fico voltando a essa comparação inútil, quase como quem tenta extrair lógica de um abismo. O tempo, que comigo pareceu hesitar, com ela foi direto. E, no fim, eu sei que nenhuma das duas saiu ilesa.


Ter trinta dias não torna a perda menor, e perder dois dias não diminui o amor que existia ali. Mas essas medidas dizem muito sobre como o tempo se comporta: ele pode ser paciente em um momento e absolutamente indiferente em outro. O tempo me permitiu acompanhar e me despedir, ainda que de forma imperfeita. Mas também me fez perdê-lo cedo demais, quando eu ainda tinha muito a viver ao lado dele.


E, quando penso na Ana Paula, penso nesse limite tão pequeno que fez toda a diferença. Dois dias que não puderam ser adiados. 48 horas que nenhum prêmio nem esforço conseguem comprar de volta. Hoje ela tem milhões, tem a vitória que buscou, mas não tem o tempo que lhe faltou.


Pra mim, em todos os lugares, culturas e economias, o tempo sempre vai ser a moeda mais valiosa que existe (e a mais injusta), porque ele se distribui de formas diferentes, sem explicar seus critérios. Dá um mês para uns, tira dois dias de outros, e, ainda assim, nunca é suficiente.


Hoje eu vivo em um meio-termo entre a gratidão e a revolta. Agradeço pelos trinta dias que tive, pelo privilégio de me despedir. Mas também me revolto com o fato de que não tive mais, e de que, no fim, o tempo decidiu encerrar a história ali, sem mais nem menos. E, quando me vem à mente a história da Ana Paula, penso que, de um jeito ou de outro, nós duas fomos atravessadas pela mesma certeza: o tempo …

author: Paola Victoria Churchill Bigal
title: Derrotas no futebol aumentam registros de violência doméstica
content:
Marcia*, de 45 anos, aprendeu a ler o calendário do Campeonato Brasileiro antes de conseguir dar nome ao que vivia. Nos dias de jogo do Corinthians, o jantar tinha que estar pronto antes de a bola rolar. As crianças iam para a casa da avó sempre que dava. Visitas, ela desmarcava com desculpas inventadas. Durante os 90 minutos, nenhuma pergunta. “Eu vivia em estado de alerta, tentando prever o humor dele e evitar qualquer situação que pudesse provocar uma explosão”, conta ela, hoje com 45 anos.


Não foi sempre assim. No começo do casamento, ela assistia aos jogos ao lado do marido, torcedor apaixonado. “Parecia algo normal, um programa de casal.” Com os anos, percebeu que os dias de partida mudavam o comportamento dele. Quando o Corinthians perdia, ele chegava nervoso, respondia gritando, dizia que ninguém o respeitava se as crianças faziam barulho. 


A primeira agressão física veio depois de um clássico perdido e de muita bebida. Marcia pediu que ele falasse mais baixo, o filho dormia. Foi empurrada contra a parede. Ele se desculpou, disse que estava de cabeça quente, jurou que nunca mais. “Mas aconteceu de novo e de novo.”


O que Marcia viveu tem tradução estatística. Um estudo das economistas Isadora Bousquat Árabe (London School of Economics e FEA-USP) e Paula Carvalho Pereda (FEA-USP), aceito para

publicação

 na revista Economic Development and Cultural Change, da Universidade de Chicago, analisou 2.105 partidas de fim de semana do Brasileirão entre 2015 e 2019 e cruzou os resultados com boletins de ocorrência de violência doméstica dentro de casa em São Paulo e no Rio de Janeiro. 


Quando o time do coração perde um jogo em que era favorito – ou seja, em que sofre uma derrota inesperada, medida pelas cotações do mercado de apostas –, os registros sobem em média 6% nas seis horas seguintes ao apito final.


O efeito não aparece antes do jogo, nem durante, nem depois de vitórias. Ele se concentra nas horas que se seguem à frustração e depois se dissipa. “Quando a gente fala de gatilho emocional, basicamente vem a decepção. A pessoa fica muito brava. Se você está ali na mesma casa, com álcool, tudo que já está propenso a explodir… isso não vai ser a causa, mas vai ser o gatilho”, disse Árabe à reportagem.


A escalada de um ciclo


O empurrão contra a parede não foi o começo da violência na casa de Marcia. Antes dele vieram os gritos, as acusações, o silêncio obrigatório dos dias de jogo. E é exatamente esse padrão que os dados capturam: 


O aumento nos registros não vem de agressões físicas isoladas, mas de boletins que somam mais de uma forma de violência no mesmo episódio. Os que combinam violência física, psicológica e moral crescem cerca de 50% a cada desvio-padrão de choque emocional negativo; os de violência psicológica e moral, cerca de 30%.


“Não é só uma violência física. Ela geralmente vem acompanhada de uma violência moral, uma difamação, uma ameaça”, diz Árabe. “São formas de o agressor controlar a vítima.”


A derrota no futebol, portanto, não cria um agressor. Ela intensifica um ciclo que já estava em curso e que a vítima, muitas vezes, já administra sozinha há anos, reorganizando a rotina da casa em função da tabela do campeonato, como fazia Marcia.


Segundo dados da Pesquisa Nacional de Violência contra a Mulher de 2025, realizada pelo Instituto DataSenado,

58% das mulheres

 que sofreram violência doméstica nos 12 meses anteriores conviviam com os abusos havia mais de um ano ao serem entrevistadas, e apenas 21% vivia o problema havia menos de seis meses. Os dados da pesquisa estão disponíveis no

Mapa Nacional da Violência de Gênero

, iniciativa da Gênero e Número, do DataSenado e do Instituto Natura.


E o aumento de 6% nos registros de violência após o final de um jogo, admitem as próprias autoras, é um piso. “Muito provavelmente subestima. É um lower bound,  (um limite inferior, ou uma estimativa mínima do efeito)”, afirma a Marcia. O motivo está num dos gráficos mais duros do estudo: em municípios sem delegacia com funcionamento 24 horas, mulheres agredidas num sábado de jogo esperam em média cerca de 40 horas para conseguir registrar a ocorrência, muitas vezes só na segunda-feira, quando a delegacia reabre.


E isso considerando apenas as que denunciam. A violência doméstica está entre os crimes mais subnotificados que existem. Também de acordo com a Pesquisa Nacional de Violência contra a Mulher de 2025,

58% das vítimas

 que haviam sofrido abusos nos últimos 12 meses não …

author: Rein Tarinay
title: Canada-Philippines ‘strategic partnership’ for whom?
content:
Hundreds protest during Ferdinand Marcos Jr’s visit in Vancouver Canada (Photo by BAYAN BC)

“Security, development, and economic growth for whom? For whom is this going to serve? It always goes to big business, to bureaucrats, to corrupt government officials, to the same people it always goes to. And we have to expose this, because this is not economic growth, security and development of the people. This is further putting the people in precarious, dangerous, exploitative conditions in both Canada and the Philippines.”

TORONTO – During last year’s State of the Nation Address (SONA), Ferdinand Marcos Jr. did not mention the unequal trade and military agreements with the United States. For this year’s SONA, as he ties up with another foreign power, progressives anticipate that Marcos Jr. will frame the agreements as yet another “achievement” of his administration.

Early July, Marcos Jr. met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Vancouver and announced the Canada-Philippines Strategic Partnership under the guise of “ deepening bilateral cooperation in trade, energy, defence, and tourism .” The two governments boasted of its people-to-people relationship and claimed it will benefit economic growth. But progressives in Canada ask, who is this really for?

A priority of the bilateral partnership is concluding negotiations on a Canada-Philippines Free Trade Agreement by the end of the year. The agreement states that Canada aims to expand agricultural and forest product exports to the Philippines where landgrabbing, extractive mining, and militarization result in the killings of farmers and human rights defenders, as per the reports of various human rights watchdogs.

In an interview with Bulatlat , Alison Matthews, chairperson of the International League of Peoples’ Struggle (ILPS) in Canada, emphasized that the unequal trade agreements that Carney and Marcos Jr. signed and ongoing talks on declaration of intent only marks continued worsening human rights violations against the Filipino people.

“Canada headquarters over half of the world’s mining companies, and many of those companies operate in the country. B2 Gold, Oceanagold , and Barrick Gold , all have projects in the Philippines, with a long history of human rights violations, including having the AFP and state militia surrounding those mines, and killing land defenders, and displacing indigenous people. These projects contaminate the water and the soil, making soil unproductive for farming, and water undrinkable, so people are forced to leave,” they told Bulatlat.

“Security, development, and economic growth for whom? For whom is this going to serve? It always goes to big business, to bureaucrats, to corrupt government officials, to the same people it always goes to. And we have to expose this, because this is not economic growth, security and development of the people. This is further putting the people in precarious, dangerous, exploitative conditions in both Canada and the Philippines,” Matthews added.

The agreement also includes a Joint Declaration of Intent on Energy and Natural Resources Cooperation . While it is still under negotiation, it signals a clear push toward increased Canadian involvement in Philippine energy and resource extraction. A Joint Declaration of Intent on Labour and Migration was also signed without amendment and wording that protects and defends migrant workers on Canada’s employer-tied temporary foreign worker system, which has left many overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) vulnerable to precarious working conditions, exploitation and abuse.

All these agreements are happening alongside the Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA).

Matthews underscored Canada’s complicity in fascist repression and exploitation of the people in the Philippines through militarization and weapons trade deals, through the SOVFA between Canada and the Philippines.

This year marks the first year that the Canadian military participated in the Balikatan war exercises further pushing Canada’s Indo-pacific strategy, which BAYAN Canada asserts would further entrench Filipinos to “militarization and state terrorism”.

“While millions of Filipinos suffer from extreme poverty, skyrocketing prices of oil, food and basic commodities,  unemployment, worsening hunger, and militarization, Marcos Jr. travels overseas to further strengthen military and economic agreements that open the Philippines to foreign plunder and intervention. These agreements are not for …

author: cnt.es
title: 27 de julio. Presentación de cómic sobre memoria histórica
content:
La CNT, en colaboración con la Fundación Anselmo Lorenzo, reedita y presenta la obra junto con su autor José Javier Pi Chevrot. La cita será el próximo lunes 27 de julio y contará con la presencia de Luis Mª Jiménez de Aberasturi Corta. Se trata de un cómic “de culto” dibujado en 1979 según “La comuna de San Sebastián” de Manuel Chiapuso.


FECHA:

 lunes 27 de julio a las 18:30 horas

LUGAR:

 librería Kaxilda (C/Arroka, Amara, Donostia)


PARTICIPANTES:


José Javier Pi Chevrot


Arquitecto, dibujante e investigador de la historia de Donostia. Publicaciones:

La ciudad de Donostia-San Sebastián antes de 1813: reivindicación de su presencia

 (2019) y

Cuando San Sebastián era base corsaria con el puerto del Pasage 1797-1813

 (2026).


Luis Mª Jiménez de Aberasturi Corta


Escritor, editor y colaborador en prensa. Entre otras publicaciones:

La guerra en Euskadi

(1978, con su hermano Juan Carlos),

Casilda, miliciana: Historia de un sentimiento

(1985).


Se cumplen ahora 90 años de unos sucesos que aún resuenan en la memoria colectiva donostiarra gracias en gran parte al relato de Chiapuso (

La comuna de San

Sebastián, 1977) y al cómic que José Javier dibujó “a plumilla” en 1979 y cuya 5ª edición presentamos ahora. A lo largo de sus páginas, aparecen militantes históricos de la CNT como Kasilda Hernáez, Félix Likiniano, Manuel Chiapuso, Valentín Alvarez, Patricio Ruiz de Galarreta o José Luis Otero.


Donostia y Barcelona fueron las dos únicas ciudades en las que el ejército se echó a la calle y fue vencido por el pueblo en armas. En ambas, la CNT y el movimiento libertario tuvieron un papel protagonista.


El 22 de julio de 1936, militares de Loiola, guardias de asalto, policías municipales y civiles fascistas avanzaban hacia el centro de la ciudad con un arsenal de guerra. Poco antes de llegar a la sede de la CNT en Larramendi, grupos de acción como

La buena voluntad

,

Los tarzanes libertarios

,

Los temerarios

,

Viva la dinamita

 y una multitud de voluntari@s se enfrentaron a ellos durante casi siete horas sin apenas medios. Docenas de revolucionari@s cayeron muert@s en las calles de Amara, pero frenaron al ejército y la hazaña volvió a repetirse el día 28 con la rendición de los cuarteles de Loiola.


Aquel verano de 1936, los ecos de la revolución social que se implantó en otros territorios llegaban hasta Gipuzkoa. El proceso colectivizador se limitó a parte de la flota pesquera de Pasaia y al control temporal de unas pocas empresas de Donostialdea. Aún y todo, ni los golpistas ni los republicanos esperaban semejante respuesta obrera organizada, los veraneantes no entendían de donde salía esa chusma y la burguesía nacionalista vasca tomaba nota para crear después la

Ertzaña

 y que no hubiera réplicas libertarias en Bizkaia.


El otoño vino plagado de detenciones, torturas, destierros, violaciones, robo de niñ@s, desapariciones forzadas, listas negras patronales… La represión fue especialmente virulenta para con la militancia anarquista y anarcosindicalista. Diego Franco y Antonio López fueron los dos últimos fusilados en Euskal Herria (Bidebieta, 1947). Lejos de rendirse, se organizaron en la clandestinidad, crearon redes de apoyo e intentaron atentar contra el general Franco en Donostia hasta en tres ocasiones. No pudo ser.


90 años después de aquel verano, negras tormentas agitan nuevamente los aires, nubes oscuras nos siguen impediendo ver y una vez más nos toca defender nuestro bien más preciado: la libertad. Rearmémonos de autogestión, acción directa, solidaridad y federalismo. ¡A las barricadas, a las barricadas! ¡Por el triunfo de la Confederación!


Borondate ona / La buena voluntad

, grupo memorialista de CNT Gipuzkoa

author: Brian Hioe
title: Recent Incident Highlights Use of Chinese Parts in Biometric Equipment in Police, Coast Guard, and Customs
content:
DPP LEGISLATOR Lin Chun-hsian publicized earlier this month that the police, coast guard, customs, and CPC Corporation are all suspected of using equipment of Chinese manufacture in biometric equipment. Such equipment was used for clocking in employees using their faces and fingerprints.

Such equipment is originally thought to be manufactured by ARMATURA, a subsidiary of ZKTeco, which is 99.98% owned by ZKTeco. That it ended up in police, coast guard, customs, and CPC use is because a Taiwanese company is suspected of rebranding and reselling the equipment. The NCC certification data for the devices, as well as their product descriptions, are identical to ARMATURA products. The instruction manual for the products, too, retains terms used in China but not Taiwan.

Reportedly, such purchases of equipment took place across a decade, with the Taiwanese company in question winning 16 tenders. Lin has called for a review of the procurement process, suggesting that designated government agencies should not be allowed to decide on purchases of equipment that store biometric or other sensitive data. Lin has also suggested an issue with the current procurement process, in that even equipment pertaining to national security must go to the lowest bidder, meaning that this incentivizes the purchase of what may be Chinese equipment.

This is hardly the first time that a Taiwanese company has been found to be passing off Chinese products as Taiwanese ones, even in government tenders that would be in the limelight. For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic, it proved an embarrassment for the Tsai administration when members of the “national team” convened to boost production of medical masks were found to be passing off Chinese-manufactured masks as Taiwanese ones.

Likewise, there have been other cases in which Chinese technology has found its way into sensitive equipment that pertains to national security. In 2022, the luggage self-check-in system for Taoyuan International Airport was found to have machinery parts and software made by the subsidiary of a Chinese arms manufacturer, China North Industries Corporation (Norinco). The machines were built in China, but then disassembled and shipped to Taiwan. The logic controller for the system was programmed by a Japanese company, but using programming originally designed by Norinco, which further leads to concerns that there could be backdoors in this software.

Indeed, this is more broadly the concern with equipment of Chinese manufacturers that is found to be widely used in Taiwan, in that there may be Chinese backdoors. The same year, there was increased scrutiny on the widespread use of Hikvision security cameras in Taiwan. Hikvision is a Chinese brand, and there were fears regarding Hikvision routing footage through Chinese servers. It was found that 1,089 Hikvision cameras were in use at 309 schools or agencies.

At the time, this pointed to a larger issue. A report by the Executive Yuan in May 2021 found that 19,256 devices made in China were used in 2,596 schools, local governments, and other institutions. 1,848 cameras or drones made by Da-Jiang Innovations Technology were used by 717 universities, and 1,632 computer networking systems were used by TP-Link Technologies. Some schools refused to remove the cameras after being informed of the issue.

In 2024, controversy broke out after banned Chinese-made parts were reported as being used at a number of army bases, in that renewable energy initiatives on bases used Chinese telecommunications devices. This included computer control systems, power inverters, and routers, which TPP legislator Huang Kuo-chang–who publicized the claims–stated were in use at the Hungchailin Army Base, National Defense University, and Naval Fleet Command. Huang framed his criticisms as showing that the pan-Green camp’s “national team” for renewable energy had allowed for Chinese United Front efforts.

Not long afterward, KMT legislator Hsu Chiao-hsin publicized that military vehicles, including for generals, used dashboard cameras manufactured in China. 800 dashcams were removed after the probe.

It can be seen, then, that the use of Chinese equipment in sensitive facilities and institutions in Taiwan continues to be a recurrent issue. At a time when Taiwan has placed great emphasis on supply chains that avoid China, and suggested to the Western world that it could be a technology hub for supply chains that avoid the use of Chinese parts on …

content:

Hur man löser hyresfrågan i Ryssland - därom berättar följande lilla meddelande, som vi mottagit från en kamrat:

I Moskwa tyckte en hyresvärd, att hans hyresgäster icke betalte tillräckligt. Förbjuden att kasta ut dem så länge kriget varar, sökte han att trötta ut dem genom att vara brutal och rå. Han hoppades så, att de skulle flytta från honom, och han skulle bli i tillfälle att beskatta de nya hyresgästerna hårdare. Han lyckades värkligen att trötta ut dem, men resultatet blev icke det åsyftade.

Hyresgästerna sammanträdde och beslutade själva taga hand om fastighetens administration. Det tillsattes en kommitté, som fick i uppdrag att uppbära hyrorna, att inköpa ved och kol till den nödiga uppvärmningen, reglera förhållandena med elektriska ljuset, låta utföra reparationer etc. Kommittén administrerade nu huset på ett sådant sätt, att alla de klagomål, som de förut varit så berättigade att resa, föllo bort. Blev det några pängar över, sedan de nödvändiga utgifterna blivit bestridda av den influtna hyran, så tillställdes dessa ägaren.

Nå, denna "lösning" är tydligen icke fullt tillfredsställande, men det är ett steg i rätt riktning. Det är icke vad vi vilja: att husen fullständigt skola ställas till hyresgästernas disposition, utan skatteplikt till privatkapitalistiska ägare eller stat, men det är en reform mot detta mål. Och exemplet är också intressant ur den synpunkten, att det visar hur den kommunistiska idéen ligger så att säga i luften överallt: gemensamhetsbruk och gemensam förvaltning. Och när hyresgästerna själva långt bättre sörjde för förvaltningen och för hyresgästernas bekvämlighet - och det var ju huvudsaken! - varför skall man så uppdraga det åt trakasseringslystna privatbesittare, som blott plundra hyresgästerna?

Det är i varje fall i denna riktning vi skola gå, för att genomföra socialiseringen av husen, av bostäderna: att undantränga de privata besittarna och sätta fastigheterna under hyresgästernas direkta administration. När revolutionen en gång väl slagit in på denna väg inom alla livets områden, när folket en gång fattar revolutionen på detta sätt, skall dess förvärkligande icke vara långt borta.

Låt oss därför akta oss för att kräva statens ingripande, och skapa ännu en byråkratisk institution, som ytterst blott tjänar till att befästa den privata besittningsrätten, och göra oss alla ännu mera avhängiga av statens förmynderskap. Den vägen blev en väg till större ofrihet blott. Låt oss själv söka att självständigt övertaga alla bourgeoisisamhällets ekonomiska funktioner. Genom oss själva och för oss själva.

Först när vi på detta sätt gör både privatkapitalismen existensrätten stridig och undantränger statens funktioner, kunna vi tänka på en praktisk realisering av samfundsomvälvningen.

title: Gülistan Doku soruşturması: Handan Sonel de tutuklandı
content:
Dersim'de 5 Ocak 2020'den bu yana kayıp olan üniversite öğrencisi Gülistan Doku'nun akıbetine ilişkin yürütülen soruşturmada dikkat çeken bir gelişme yaşandı. Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan eski Tunceli Valisi Tuncay Sonel'in eşi Handan Sonel ile Doku'nun telefonuna müdahale edildiği iddia edilen bilişim şirketinin sahibi Mehmet Aca tutuklandı.


Dersim ve Erzurum Cumhuriyet başsavcılıklarının talimatıyla Elazığ, Malatya, Ankara, İstanbul ve Dersim eş zamanlı operasyonlar düzenlendi. Operasyonlarda gözaltına alınan 15 şüpheliden 10'unun jandarma ve emniyetteki işlemleri tamamlandı.


Handan Sonel tutuklandı


Sağlık kontrolünün ardından adliyeye sevk edilen eski Tunceli Valisi Tuncay Sonel'in eşi Handan Sonel, Gülistan Doku dosyasındaki delillerle ilgili yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında "suç delillerini yok etme, gizleme veya değiştirme" suçlamasıyla çıkarıldığı mahkemece tutuklandı.


Doku Ailesi'nin avukatı Ali Çimen şu bilgiyi paylaştı:


"Gülistan DOKU dosyasında şüpheli Handan SONEL tutuklandı. Bu tutuklama ile birlikte dosyada toplam tutuklu sayısı 16 oldu.

#Örtbas


#Gülistandoku


#Gülistandokunerede"


Bilişim şirketi sahibi de cezaevine gönderildi


Doku'nun cep telefonuna hukuka aykırı şekilde müdahale edildiği değerlendirilen bilişim şirketinin sahibi Mehmet Aca da savcılık sorgusunun ardından nöbetçi sulh ceza hâkimliğine sevk edildi. Aca, "bilişim sistemine hukuka aykırı olarak girme veya orada kalma" ile "suç delillerini yok etme, gizleme veya değiştirme" suçlarından tutuklandı.


Bu tutuklamalarla birlikte soruşturma kapsamında tutuklanan kişi sayısı 16'ya yükseldi.


Korucubaşı Y.A.'nın sorgusu sürüyor


Soruşturma kapsamında adliyeye sevk edilen eski güvenlik korucubaşı Y.A.'nın ise savcılıktaki sorgusunun sürdüğü öğrenildi.

author: David Swanson
title: World BEYOND War Supports WILPF’s 34th International Congress in Cameroon
content:
By Guy Feugap, Africa Organizer of World BEYOND War


For four days from 17 to 20 July 2026, Cameroon hosted the 34th international congress of the Women’s International League for Peace and Freedom (WILPF). Organized by the WILPF Cameroon section in a hybrid format, the congress, WILPF’s highest decision-making body, marked an important milestone for both Cameroon and the global feminist peace movement. Delegates from more than forty national sections elected a new International Board, re-elected Cameroonian peace leader Sylvie Jacqueline Ndongmo as International President, and committed again to advancing feminist peace in a world increasingly affected by war, militarization and injustice. World BEYOND War supported WILPF Cameroon in organizing this event.


Hosting the Congress in Cameroon carried a symbolic significance. Although often perceived as a relatively stable country in Africa, Cameroon has been deeply affected by multiple and overlapping crises. Armed conflict in the North-West and South-West regions, violent extremism in the Far North, the arrival of refugees from neighboring countries, and intercommunal and political tensions have all placed immense pressure on communities, with women and children bearing a disproportionate share of the consequences. As WILPF Cameroon President Nathalie Wokam Foko noted in her opening address,

“Women are too often the first to experience displacement, widowhood, economic hardship, and violence, yet they are also among the first to rebuild peace”

.


Against this backdrop, bringing the international feminist peace movement to Yaoundé was far more than a logistical choice. It demonstrated confidence in the leadership and resilience of WILPF in Cameroon while sending the message that peacebuilding must take place where its impact is most urgently needed. The congress also created an opportunity for representatives of the Cameroonian government, civil society, traditional and religious leaders, international partners, and peace advocates from Cameroon and around the world to come together around the shared vision that sustainable peace can only be achieved through dialogue, justice, inclusion, and the meaningful participation of women.


Sylvie Jacqueline Ndongmo Re-elected to Lead WILPF for a New 3-Years Term


One of the defining moments of the congress was the re-election of Sylvie Jacqueline Ndongmo of Cameroon as International President of WILPF for a new three-year term, with 78% of votes. WILPF members from around the world continue to place confidence in her, upon recognizing that under her leadership, WILPF has strengthened its commitment to feminist peace, disarmament, and justice while expanding collaboration across regions and movements.


For Cameroon, Sylvie’s re-election is also a source of national pride. Founder of WILPF Cameroon, she has spent a decade building the section into one of the movement’s most active and respected. From advancing the Women, Peace and Security agenda to promoting peace education and early warning mechanisms, supporting internally displaced women, her work has demonstrated that local action influences global peacebuilding.


World BEYOND War’s Contribution to the Congress


As a partner of WILPF Cameroon, World BEYOND War was invited and provided support for the organization. Representing WBW, I joined the congress organizing team, where I contributed to several key aspects of the event. My responsibilities included supporting logistical coordination, facilitating communication among organizers, moderating selected congress sessions, and serving on the Peace Team, a volunteer group responsible for fostering dialogue, responding to tensions, and helping ensure that the congress remained a safe, respectful, and collaborative space for all participants. The congress was more than an organizational milestone. Bringing this global gathering to Cameroon demonstrated that countries facing complex security challenges are not merely places where peace is needed; they are also places where innovative solutions, resilient communities, and transformative leadership emerge. For us, supporting this Congress was not simply about helping organize an event, but about standing alongside a partner whose work demonstrates that feminist leadership, nonviolent action, and community-based peacebuilding are essential to building a world beyond war.

title: How Letter Carriers Can Organize to Prevent Smoke Injury
content:
Letter carriers and other people who work outdoors, especially in the upper Midwest and East, are experiencing hazardous levels of smoke from Canadian wildfires. Some areas have been experiencing AQI (Air Quality Index) measurements of over 300, even over 500, with local authorities advising residents to stay indoors.


As temperatures continue to rise from climate change and vegetation dries out and catches fire from lightning, this situation will get worse.


We are being given advice by Postal Service management and our union leadership to make individual decisions about whether we are safe delivering mail in these conditions. Wrong! We are berated with the slogan “Safety Depends on Me!” Wrong!


Management should be following local health advisories and keep carriers off the street in these conditions. But reports from carriers all over the Midwest let us know that management is instructing carriers to deliver the mail and use a mask if desired and available. Wrong!


Many carriers will follow management instructions despite concern for their own or co-workers’ safety because they fear management retaliation if they do not—especially people in the more vulnerable job categories of City Carrier Associates and Part-Time Flexible employees.


Or they assume that they will not be impacted by the smoke. (Hint: wildfire smoke inhalation can damage healthy individuals over time; see the last section of this article.)


Or they do not want to be considered weak when others are going ahead. Or they don’t want to bring back mail to have to face overburdened days to come.


THE ANSWER: COLLECTIVE ACTION


What is to be done? Collective action to protect all carriers, together, in the area. Here’s a step-by-step approach:


Educate carriers on their right to refuse to work outdoors when there is serious smoke from wildfires,

 using stand-up meetings, flyers, bulletin boards, and breakroom meet-ups.


The criterion for when mail delivery is unsafe is

not

 only when there is a “risk of death or serious bodily injury.”


We have the right to avoid

any

 illness or injury caused by unsafe air quality, which can be predicted by Air Quality Index and is scientifically proven (see the last section of this article).


Even the USPS directives, distributed as stand-ups in late July, state, “Those who are most at risk are… active people of all ages who exercise or work vigorously outdoors…”


Demand (by circulating a petition or speaking up at a stand-up meeting) that management supply every carrier with an N95 or P100 mask.

 If necessary, use multiple 1767 Hazardous Condition and Article 14 Safety and Health grievances with evidence from local authorities or nearby AQI readings.


Get all carriers in your station or your area on a WhatsApp chat.


Assign carriers to monitor air quality index

 (AQI at

AirNow.gov

) and keep track of local authorities’ directives.


Decide together (consulting AirNow.gov) how the group should respond to certain AQI levels,

 i.e. when to refuse to go out without N95 or P100 masks, when carriers with respiratory conditions should bring the mail back, when everyone should bring the mail back, etc.


Talk through the consequences if everyone brings the mail back.

 Will management discipline all of us? Can we threaten to go public if they try? What if mail piles up and takes a while to get delivered?


When alerted by the monitors, spread the word of AirNow.gov advice and indicate that “many carriers may want to” bring the mail back.

 Prepare carriers for these words that allow “plausible deniability,” i.e. you are not calling for a strike, only for carriers to be safe.


When bringing the mail back, fill out form 1767 (hazardous conditions) describing the specific hazardous conditions

 (e.g. AQI and/or local authority directives).


Also fill out form 1571 (undelivered mail) describing the mail curtailed. Inform management that you will not work outside but that you are available to work inside. Do not leave until your shift is over or until directed by management (fill out form 3971 for Administrative Leave).


HEALTH RISKS OVER TIME


Wildfire smoke inhalation can damage healthy individuals over time. The smoke contains a high concentration of fine particulate matter and toxic pollutants. These ultrafine particles penetrate deep into the lungs, enter the bloodstream, and trigger systemic inflammation and oxidative stress, which can lead to cumulative cardiovascular and respiratory risks, as …

Los años 30s fueron un verdadero tutorial sobre cómo se desactiva una rebelión.

author: Beryl Lipton
title: Hundreds of Drone-as-First-Responder Programs Could Soon Be Launched Across the Country
content:
Police departments across the country are lining up to launch drone-as-first-responder (DFR) programs, and hundreds have cleared a necessary hurdle toward making deployment a reality, expanding aerial surveillance and data collection even in areas patrol officers typically can't reach.

As of February 2026, over 1,000 public safety agencies—including police, fire, and other emergency management agencies—had received Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) waivers needed to automate drone operations and launch a DFR program, according to a recent Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) release listing agencies that have obtained Part 91 waivers since the FAA streamlined and sped up the process in April 2025.

The changes led to a massive increase in the number of waivers issued. Only 976 DFR waivers had been granted since the first DFR program launched in 2018 through April 2025, according to an FAA representative. The agency issued more waivers between April 2025 and February 2026 than it had in the previous seven years combined.

A map illustrating the locations of police departments and other public safety agencies that have received Part 91 waivers, making it possible for them to launch drone-as-first-responder programs. (This map image links to Google Maps, which is governed by Google's privacy policy)

The new FAA process for waivers and the rush of police departments to obtain them signifies a shift in law enforcement's use of drones: from human-operated aerial surveillance to AI-based autonomous drone use.

Typically, a drone operator is only permitted to fly in areas that can still be seen by the pilot, and that drone pilot needs to be certified under FAA Part 107. To fly drones “Beyond Visual Line of Sight” (BVLOS) requires additional approval from the FAA, as do flights above 200 feet, due to the risk of colliding with planes and other aircrafts. Without such approval, an officer could not pilot a drone from a desk inside a building and fly it to a call across the city because they could not possibly have line of sight on the drone.

FAA rules for police drones also required a human operator to manually fly the device to a scene, but DFR technology has become a more common and more automated police technology. DFR programs increasingly rely on artificial intelligence to automate drone flights from launchpads placed around the city, often atop municipal buildings, and make it possible for one drone operator to “fly” multiple devices at once. Though not every police department that has received BVLOS has launched a DFR program yet, by going through this process, every department on this list has signified it has strong enough interest to clear the necessary regulatory hurdles.

Police departments and the companies that sell DFR equipment claim that these drones make it easier for officers to establish “situational awareness” of a scene before they arrive. Early drone adoption centered on similar claims, particularly related to high-risk situations like vehicular accidents or incidents involving an armed suspect. However, these kinds of situations may make up only a small portion of deployments, which often occur in response to low-risk calls for service related to unhoused people, mental health concerns, and loud music, as a Government Technology analysis of the system in Chula Vista, California, found.

DFR programs have become important sources of revenue for companies like Flock Safety and Axon, the latter of which reported that its DFR platform has become one of the company’s fastest growing sectors. Axon is also known for products like the TASER and the Fusus camera system that lets police integrate viewing of public and private cameras.

Footage from drone flights is streamed back to a police office, and it can be stored, shared, and analyzed like other video. Turning drone footage into fodder for automated license plate reader (ALPR) networks, for example, requires very little additional software, and Flock Safety was quietly able to turn its drones into “flying ALPRs” last year.

The normalization of police DFR programs jeopardizes privacy in communities across the country. As flying cameras, drones can capture footage from areas typically inaccessible to a casual patrol officer—backyards, roofs, through windows—at distances that leave subjects of surveillance completely unaware of the spy in the sky. A recent leak of drone footage from the San Francisco Police Department illustrated the ease with which …

Una nueva protesta de jubilados, esta vez con el acompañamiento de las tres centrales (CGT y las CTAs), elevó el piso de participación que se realiza miércoles tras miércoles. De la jornada también participaron movimientos sociales y organizaciones de izquierdas y de vertiente peronista.

comenzó a la mañana con la movilización de organizaciones sociales y piqueteras contra el cierre del programa Volver al Trabajo

, delegaciones de sindicatos de las tres centrales obreras de la República Argentina se hicieron presentes en la ronda de jubiladas y jubilados de todos los miércoles.


Entre ellas hubo gremios que asistieron, quizás, por primera vez, y otros como La Bancaria, ATE y Camioneros que además de estar presentes con una columna importante, son participantes frecuentes. Y, en el caso de los conducidos por Moyano, asisten a las y los jubilados con ollas populares cada miércoles. Es un gesto de solidaridad que aporta a la lucha y permite que muchos de los manifestantes puedan contar con una comida caliente, que se suma al aporte de los hinchas y algunos otros gremios, que vienen reuniendo y distribuyendo alimentos en las rondas.

La jornada del miércoles dejó varios aspectos para destacar. En primer lugar, se registró una importante participación tanto del sector peronista como de las organizaciones de izquierda, lo que evidenció un amplio espectro político confluyendo en el reclamo. Sin embargo, más allá de la diversidad política, lo que realmente convoca a muchos adultos mayores fue la urgencia alimentaria.


Según relató el Chaca, referente de los jubilados, las organizaciones están realizando un esfuerzo para cubrir al menos dos comidas al mes por persona, a través de la entrega de bolsones de alimentos. En ese sentido, destacó que cada vez es más frecuente la presencia de jubiladas y jubilados que antes no participaban de las movilizaciones y que ahora asisten exclusivamente para buscar el bolsón de comida.

Todo esto ocurre en un contexto de profunda crisis para el sector. Las y los jubilados atraviesan una situación crítica signada por el congelamiento de los bonos – en $70.000- y el aumento permanente de la canasta básica. Para julio de 2026, la jubilación mínima con bono ronda los $481.948, tras una actualización del 2,1%, muy por debajo de la inflación real. A esto se suma una caída del 50% en las nuevas altas previsionales, lo que profundiza el desamparo de quienes intentan acceder al sistema. El ajuste también golpea las atenciones del PAMI y la entrega de medicamentos, dos pilares fundamentales para la salud de los adultos mayores.

Online Webinar

Sunday July 26th, 2026

2:00PM ET / 11:00AM PT

Online Registration: 

https://withfriends.co/event/28287878/General_Admission

 

Watch live and thereafter: 

https://www.youtube.com/@CommonNotions

 


One day our comrades will come home. Leonard Peltier came home last year;

Marius Mason

came home this year. Many of our Green Scare, Animal Rights, Anarchist, Black and Puerto Rican Liberation, Indigenous and Anti-Imperialist Warriors, and Conscientious Objectors have come home. And one day the Prairieland and other anti-fascist prisoners will return to our communities, too.


Join the Dallas-Fort Worth (DFW) Support Committee and friends for an online webinar, Sunday, July 26, at 2pm ET, as we celebrate Marius Mason’s return home and let those inside know we are here for them. MC’d by Matt Meyer with Ashanti Alston, Diana Block, Josh Harper, Ray Luc Levasseur, and Julie Herrada (Marius Mason Support Committee). 


People Do Come Home: An Event for the Prairieland Defendants and All Political Prisoners brings together an inter-generational group of former political prisoners and support committee members who will share their experiences of coming home and building prisoner support movements as we seek solace in a time of fascism. 


“For, if they take you in the morning,” James Baldwin wrote to Angela Davis, “they will be coming for us that night.” Our movement must respond as “they” may come for “us”: repress us, arrest us, imprison us. But we will fight back and be here for each other when we come home!


While this is a free event, we humbly ask that you donate to the Marius Mason Support Fund at

https://supportmariusmason.org/support/

 


# # #  


The full event will be transcribed and shared with political prisoners and made available to support committees.

title: Gran jornada nacional de lucha contra la baja del programa Volver al Trabajo
content:
Este miércoles se vivió una gran jornada de lucha y movilización en todo el territorio nacional. Por la mañana, los movimientos sociales y organizaciones piqueteras realizaron marchas, cortes de ruta y ollas populares en todo el país en rechazo al cierre del programa Volver al Trabajo, que deja a más de 900 mil familias sin el mísero aporte que les permitía subsistir. El gobierno nacional de ultraderecha mandó a reprimirlos en Avellaneda, y hubo despliegue de fuerzas federales en otros territorios, como Gendarmería en Rosario.

Por la tarde, se realizó la marcha al Congreso en apoyo a la lucha de las y los jubilados

.


La represión en Avellaneda


Organizaciones sociales y territoriales nucleadas en la Unión de Trabajadores y Trabajadoras de la Economía Popular (UTEP), el Frente de Lucha Piquetero y Territorios en Lucha, realizaron en la mañana del miércoles 22 una gran Jornada Nacional de Lucha con cortes de rutas, movilizaciones y asambleas en distintos puntos del país para exigir que el gobierno de Javier Milei dé marcha atrás con la baja del programa Volver al Trabajo.


La principal concentración tuvo lugar en la base del Puente Pueyrredón, en Avellaneda, provincia de Buenos Aires, mientras se realizaron acciones simultáneas en

al menos quince provincias

.


La convocatoria denunció el desmantelamiento del programa reclamando que “Trabajo sin salario es esclavitud”, exigiendo la continuidad del beneficio para quienes sostienen tareas comunitarias en comedores, merenderos, cooperativas y espacios comunitarios en barrios populares.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Represion-en-Puente-Pueyrredon-01-PO.mp4


Video: Partido Obrero


En Avellaneda, invocando el inconstitucional protocolo antiprotesta, la Policía Federal y la Prefectura Naval avanzaron contra las y los manifestantes para impedirles que crucen a pie el Puente Pueyrredón, que conecta Avellaneda con la Capital Federal.


Eduardo Belliboni, referente del Polo Obrero, fue uno de los más afectados por los gases. “La infame Prefectura que en lugar de cuidar las fronteras contra el narco, está gaseando la manifestación de miles de trabajadores de Volver al Trabajo que fueron despedidos. A metros de la estación Darío y Maxi. ¡Cobardes! Viva la lucha piquetera”, declaró.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Represion-en-Puente-Pueyrredon-01-Canal-Abierto.mp4


Video: Canal Abierto


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Represion-en-Puente-Pueyrredon-03-PO.mp4


“Muestren la orden para tirarle a un par de mamás con hijos”, interpeló una trabajadora de uno de los comedores populares de la Matanza a los efectivos de Prefectura Naval que reprimieron en Avellaneda. 

Video: Prensa Obrera


Asimismo, las fuerzas impidieron el acceso a la Ciudad de Buenos Aires de manifestantes que marchaban por la avenida Maipú en el partido de Vicente López, para cruzar y cortar la zona de Puente Saavedra y circular hacia el centro porteño.


Los movimientos sociales habían anticipado que se sumarían al acto de protesta que desde las 15 se llevó a cabo en la zona del Congreso convocada por la CGT y las dos CTA, entre otras organizaciones, para acompañar la marcha de los miércoles de los jubilados para protestar contra las políticas del Gobierno nacional.


En Mar del Plata las y los manifestantes cortaron la autovía 2 en el acceso a la ciudad, entre la rotonda de ingreso a la ciudad y el acceso al aeropuerto, sobre los barrios La Florida y 2 de abril.


En San Juan,

la Radio Comunitaria La Lechuza, integrante de FARCO, entrevistó al dirigente de la UTEP Fidel Maric

, quien expresó: “Entre 15.000 y 20.000 sanjuaninos se quedarían sin ese ingreso, lo que significa también una baja de inyección líquida de recursos en la economía popular, en la economía cotidiana de los barrios populares, que ronda los 1.500 o 1.600 millones de pesos”.


En Córdoba también unieron sus reclamos los movimientos sociales, centrales sindicales y jubilados. Allí, Radio Sur habló con uno de los jubilados presentes: “Hace dos años y medio, éramos nosotros y las palomas solamente en la plaza. Hoy la hemos llenado la plaza, la hemos llenado de lucha, la lucha de convicciones. Y acá frente al Pami, estamos presentes y vamos por más”.
